---
title: "Troubleshooting"
---

A hook misbehaved. There is no `doctor` command. You diagnose with two tools, the dispatch logs and a re-run of your inline tests.

## Diagnostic commands

Reach for these first. The logs show what dispatch actually saw; the tests show what your conditions match.

```bash
uvx capt-hook logs                          # Print the most recent session's log
uvx capt-hook logs --tail 40                # Show only the last 40 lines
uvx capt-hook logs --session <id-or-path>   # Target a specific session (id, or transcript path)
uvx capt-hook --hooks <dir> test            # Re-run inline tests; prints the Input and PASS/FAIL
uvx capt-hook --hooks <dir> test --json     # One record per test: id, status, expected, reason
```

`logs` reads from the log directory, which defaults to `~/.cache/captain-hook/logs`. Each session writes one log file there. To target a past session, pass its id, or pass the transcript path and `logs` hashes it for you. See [Configuration](configuration.qmd#log-directory) to relocate the directory.

If a hook never appears in the log, dispatch never reached it. Work through "It never fires" below.

## Is my hook firing?

Confirm three things, in order.

First, re-run the inline tests.

```bash
uvx capt-hook --hooks <dir> test
```

Each test prints the `Input` it built and a PASS or FAIL. A FAIL means your conditions don't match the input you expect, so fix the condition before you touch dispatch. If the test passes but the hook still seems dead, move on.

Second, check that `--hooks` points at the directory holding your hook file. Captain-hook loads `.py` files under that root and nothing else.

Third, read the session log.

```bash
uvx capt-hook logs --tail 40
```

A firing hook leaves a dispatch line here. If you see the event arrive but no line for your hook, a condition skipped it. If you see no event at all, the hook is wired to the wrong event or the settings never reached Claude Code.

## It fires too often

A hook that fires on every event, or twice per event, is matching too broadly. Tighten it three ways.

Narrow the conditions. Add a `skip_if` for the cases you want to spare, or a tighter `only_if` glob. A `FilePath("**/*.py")` matches every Python file in the project; `FilePath("src/**/*.py")` matches only your source tree. See the [conditions cheatsheet](../reference/conditions.qmd) for every condition and the [conditions guide](conditions.qmd) for how to combine them.

Cap the count. For `nudge`, pass `max_fires=N` so it emits at most `N` times per session. The LLM primitives already default to a low cap, with `llm_gate` at 1 and `llm_nudge` at 3. See the [primitives reference](../reference/primitives.qmd).

Check the event set. A hook registered with `Event.Stop | Event.SubagentStop` fires on both. Confirm that both belong by reading the [events reference](../reference/events.qmd).

## It never fires

The hook is silent because dispatch never matched it. Check four causes.

Wrong event. Each primitive defaults to one event, so `block_command` targets `PreToolUse` and `nudge` targets `PostToolUse`. If you need a different one, pass `events=` explicitly. The [events reference](../reference/events.qmd) lists which event fires when.

Unsatisfiable conditions. An `only_if` is AND, so every condition must match at once. A hook with `only_if=[Tool("Bash"), FilePath("**/*.py")]` never fires, because a Bash command carries no file path. Run `uvx capt-hook --hooks <dir> test` and read the `Input` each test built against your conditions.

Settings not re-wired. After you add or change events, re-register the hooks so Claude Code knows to call your hook. This writes `.claude/settings.local.json` for you, merging non-destructively with what's already there.

```bash
uvx capt-hook --hooks <dir> register-hooks
```

Project not reloaded. Claude Code reads hook settings at session start. After you rewire settings, start a fresh session so the new wiring loads.

## Case study, a block that caught a safe command

You add a hook that blocks `git stash`, because your team uses `jj` instead.

```python
from captain_hook import hook, Event, Tool, Command

hook(
    Event.PreToolUse,
    message="Use jj shelve instead of git stash",
    block=True,
    only_if=[Tool("Bash"), Command(r"git\s+stash")],
)
```

The block works. It also blocks `git stash pop`, because `git\s+stash` is a substring of `git stash pop` and `Command` matches anywhere in the command text. Popping a stash is safe, so the hook now blocks a command you want to allow.

Fix it with a `skip_if`, which is checked first and skips the hook on any match. List the safe subcommands there.

```python
hook(
    Event.PreToolUse,
    message="Use jj shelve instead of git stash",
    block=True,
    only_if=[Tool("Bash"), Command(r"git\s+stash")],
    skip_if=[Command(r"git\s+stash\s+(pop|apply|list|show)")],
)
```

Now the safe subcommands pass through while a bare `git stash` still blocks. A re-run of `uvx capt-hook --hooks <dir> test` with a test for each subcommand confirms the split.

## NlpSignal hooks need the spaCy model

Hooks that use `NlpSignal` need the `en_core_web_sm` spaCy model. Captain-hook does not auto-download it at hook execution time, because that would trigger a silent fetch of around 100MB mid-session. Install it once with one command.

```bash
python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm
```

The form below caches it where captain-hook looks for it.

```bash
python -c "from captain_hook.util.model_cache import ensure_spacy_model; ensure_spacy_model()"
```

A missing model raises `RuntimeError: spaCy model 'en_core_web_sm' is not installed` when the hook runs.
